text: By 2040, many experts predict we will achieve Artificial General Intelligence, or AGI. Unlike today’s specialized AI, which excels at single tasks like translation or chess, AGI would match human cognitive abilities across any domain. The potential benefits are enormous: AGI could accelerate medical research, solve complex climate problems, and automate tedious labor, freeing humans for creative work. However, risks are equally serious—job displacement, misuse in warfare, or loss of control over systems smarter than us. Timeline predictions vary wildly, from optimistic 2030s to cautious late-century estimates. Regardless of the date, our collective actions today will decide whether AGI becomes humanity’s greatest tool or its final challenge.
